examples.vi: Cậu ấy nháy mắt với em trai bên bàn ăn để cùng chia sẻ trò đùa.

senses.vi: nháy mắt; nháy mắt ra hiệu

senses.definition: To shine with a light that quickly turns on and off; to twinkle.

examples.en: Distant stars winked brightly in the clear night sky.
examples.vi: Những ngôi sao xa xăm nhấp nháy sáng ngời trên bầu trời đêm quang đãng.

thesaurus.definition: signal by winking
gleam or glow intermittently
briefly shut the eyes
keep back by blinking

vi_block: Nháy mắt, nháy mắt ra hiệu.
Lấy lánh, nhấp nháy (ngọn đèn, sao).
Biểu lộ bằng cái nháy mắt.

examples: He winked at me. She winked her eye. He winked his assent.
wiktionary.gloss: To blink with only one eye as a message, signal, or suggestion, usually with an implication of conspiracy. (When transitive, the object may be the eye being winked, or the message being conveyed.)

examples: Her kitchen is a series of Still Lives; the copper pans wink on the walls.
wiktionary.gloss: To gleam fitfully or intermittently; to twinkle; to flicker.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English wynken, from Old English wincian (“to wink, make a sign, close the eyes, blink”, weak verb), from Proto-West Germanic *winkōn (“to close one's eyes”), from Proto-Indo-European *weng- (“to bow, bend, arch, curve”). Cognate with Middle Low German winken (“to blink, wink”), German winken (“to nod, beckon, make a sign”). Related also to Saterland Frisian wäänke, Dutch wenken (“to beckon, motion”), Latin vacillare (“sway”), Lithuanian véngti (“to swerve, avoid”), Albanian vang (“tire, felloe”), Sanskrit वङ्गति (vaṅgati, “(he, she) limps”), French guigner (“to eye, sneak a look at”).

senses.definition: An act of quickly closing and opening one eye as a signal.

examples.en: With a quick wink, she confirmed that the surprise party was ready.
examples.vi: Với một cái nháy mắt nhanh, cô ấy xác nhận bữa tiệc bất ngờ đã sẵn sàng.

senses.vi: cái nháy mắt; sự nháy mắt

senses.definition: A very short period of sleep.

examples.en: I did not get a wink of sleep because of the loud music.
examples.vi: Tôi không chợp mắt được chút nào vì tiếng nhạc quá ồn.

thesaurus.definition: a very short time (as the time it takes the eye to blink or the heart to beat)
closing one eye quickly as a signal
a reflex that closes and opens the eyes rapidly

wiktionary.gloss: An act of winking (a blinking of only one eye), or a message sent by winking.
A brief period of sleep; especially forty winks.
A brief time; an instant.

examples: It’s many’s the time I shot the selfsame rifiie before, and it’s many ’s the time after, but niver a wink of the same have I seen. 'T was the sight of a lifetime.
wiktionary.gloss: The smallest possible amount.

examples: The film includes a wink to wartime rationing.
wiktionary.gloss: A subtle allusion.
Synonym of tiddlywink (“small disc used in the game of tiddlywinks”).
Synonym of periwinkle (“type of mollusk”).

idioms.gloss: The hint, suggestion etc. can be understood without further explanation.
idioms.phrase: a nod is as good as a wink

idioms.gloss: A phrase used to hint that the speaker is euphemistically referring to something else.

idioms.gloss: To give (somebody) a hint or suggestion, as if by a wink; to ask or tell surreptitiously.
In a speedy or fast manner.

known: a nod is as good as a wink
a nod is as good as a wink to a blind horse
in the wink of an eye

phrasal_verbs.gloss: To turn a blind eye to (something); to corruptly ignore (some wrongdoing); to pretend not to have seen (something); to signal one's approval of (illicit activities) while maintaining the ability to plausibly deny knowing about it; to tolerate or tacitly encourage (inappropriate, immoral or illegal behavior).
to come to an end; to stop

blocks.etymology: Inherited from Middle English wrattheful, wrathful; by surface analysis, wrath + ful.

thesaurus.definition: vehemently incensed and condemnatory

wiktionary.gloss: Possessed of great wrath; very angry.

blocks.etymology: From international scientific vocabulary, from French xanthine, reflecting New Latin combining forms: xanth- + -ine; ultimately from Ancient Greek ξανθός (xanthós, “yellow”), because xanthine is yellowish-white. By surface analysis, xanth- + -ine.

thesaurus.definition: crystalline oxidation product of the metabolism of nucleoproteins; precursor of uric acid; found in many organs and in urine

wiktionary.gloss: Any of a group of alkaloids that include caffeine, theophylline, and theobromine as well as the parent compound, a precursor of uric acid found in many organs of the body.

blocks.etymology: From Spanish yerba. Doublet of herb.

wiktionary.gloss: Ilex paraguariensis, a species of holly native to southern South America; or the dried leaves and twigs of this plant, used to make the caffeine-rich beverage maté.
